name: Baby Puke Green
lede: Baby Puke Green is a bright, sour yellow-green named for infant vomit, among the most vivid of the scatological and bodily-fluid names the 2010 xkcd color survey gave this corner of green.

sections.title: A crowd name for a bodily comparison
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Who typed "baby puke green" first is undocumented; the survey records only the winning name, not its author [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a vivid yellow green, about 5.5 units off, with Munsell notation 2.6GY 7.5/10.8 [1].

The closest look-alike in our data is [[snot|Snot]], 2.6 units away, with [[puke-yellow|Puke Yellow]] and [[vomit-yellow|Vomit Yellow]] also close; [[mustard-green|Mustard Green]] sits nearby but darker [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 difference of 4, as photographed [2]. That describes the particular museums and works in this archive, not painting as a whole, and bright acid yellow-greens of this kind are simply rare in historical pigments [2].
